component: Experimental generation of Metal kernels from ordinary checked NEX scalar functions

source_path.input: Selected compiler checks current source and exports a saved language0.28 nex.graph/2 at the exact check revision.
source_path.lowering: Emit MSL from canonical typed function definitions, including the ordinary compiler contract helpers; no second source parser.

verified_semantics: Add/subtract/multiply/divide/remainder/negate and comparisons across both i64 endpoints, signed edges and deterministic full-width integer inputs.
Unsigned-bit checked arithmetic avoids Metal signed-overflow undefined behavior; division truncates toward zero and MIN modulo -1 is zero.
Arguments and operands evaluate once left-to-right; lazy boolean right operands remain conditional. First arithmetic trap ordering agrees with actual reference/native diagnostics.
Branches, mutable locals and lexical shadowing, loops, ordinary and concrete generic calls, unit roots/helpers, source pre/postconditions and loop contracts.
Only reachable function code enters the shader; an unused string and unsupported unused floating function are absent.
Finite loop under a low explicit GPU step bound reports E_GPU_STEP_LIMIT; an adequate bound matches reference/native. The GPU step metric is separate from CPU task accounting.
Noncanonical bool input is rejected per lane; eight arguments and32768 zero-argument lanes execute physically.
retained_attempts: First three-way comparison expected JSON integer tokens, while NEX correctly emitted exact decimal i64 strings. The harness expectation was fixed; the original outputs and four input files are retained.

The first generated call-depth fixture named one helper f64, a reserved source type. Generated helper names were corrected; all14 backend rejection requirements were retained. Original inputs/diagnostics are preserved.
The initial three-input physical prerequisite used the earlier runner with a deprecated Metal compile-option warning; the final runner uses current safe mathMode and precise functions.
pending: Connect generated kernels to the persistent owned NEX task/device provider, preserving admission, cancellation/deadline, physical completion, resource parents, copied-call budgets and trap behavior.
Public compiler discovery/CLI, exact graph/source diagnostic mapping, debug/profile integration and immutable relocated/archive-restored SDK delivery.
F64, aggregates, closures, recursion, source-error/finally support, remaining general GPU/NPU backends and Apple NPU.
All remaining original PLAN requirements, platform delivery, mobile/native UI, Studio, conversion, real multi-LLM costs and final main publication/cleanup.
limitations: This is an external experimental scalar backend and a physical native test harness; it is not yet GPU execution inside an ordinary NEX task application.
Raw graph evidence can include unrelated source; only kernel.metal is emitted device code.
This finite, nonisolated numerical comparison establishes neither a universal proof nor a GPU speedup.
